sentences.en: The New York Times, celebrating 175 years of helping you understand the world and make the most of each day.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》，庆祝175年来帮助您了解世界并充分利用每一天。

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Rachel Abrams and this is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的雷切尔·艾布拉姆斯，这是《每日新闻》节目。

sentences.en: After the Supreme Court overturned Roe versus Wade, abortions in the United States actually went up.
sentences.zh: 在最高法院推翻“罗诉韦德案”后，美国的堕胎数量实际上反而上升了。

sentences.en: In part, that's because of a novel legal strategy that ended up pitting blue states against red states.
sentences.zh: 部分原因是由于一种新颖的法律策略，最终导致蓝州与红州针锋相对。

sentences.en: Today, my colleague Pam Bellick explains the strategy and the two cases that could take it apart.
sentences.zh: 今天，我的同事帕姆·贝利克将解释这一策略，以及可能将其瓦解的两起案件。

sentences.en: It's Tuesday, May 27th.
sentences.zh: 今天是5月27日，星期二。

sentences.en: So Pam, we haven't talked about abortion on the show for a while.
sentences.zh: 帕姆，我们节目已经有一段时间没谈过堕胎问题了。

sentences.en: And in the years since Roe versus Wade fell, the country has kind of splintered into states where abortion is banned and states where abortion is not banned.
sentences.zh: 在“罗诉韦德案”被推翻后的几年里，这个国家分裂成了禁止堕胎的州和不禁止堕胎的州。

sentences.en: And that's just sort of been the state of play, that everybody has their own state laws that they have to abide by.
sentences.zh: 这就是目前的状况，每个人都必须遵守各自州的法律。

sentences.en: But in reality, as you have been paying attention to and covering, there's actually been this
sentences.zh: 但实际上，正如你一直关注和报道的那样，其实正在酝酿一场对峙，

sentences.en: showdown brewing that now looks poised to upend that whole order that we've maybe grown a bit accustomed to in the last few years.
sentences.zh: 这场对峙现在看来可能会颠覆我们过去几年已经习以为常的整个秩序。

sentences.en: Yeah, a lot has been happening during this time beyond the different ballot measures that we've been hearing and different state laws and things like that.
sentences.zh: 是的，这段时间发生了很多事情，除了我们听到的各种投票措施和不同的州法律之外。

sentences.en: One of the major developments has been these new legal protections called SHIELD laws.
sentences.zh: 其中一个重大进展是这些被称为“盾牌法”的新法律保护措施。

sentences.en: And they have become both one of the biggest legal developments in the abortion access space
sentences.zh: 它们不仅成为了堕胎准入领域最大的法律进展之一，

sentences.en: and also a major reason why women in states with abortion bans are still able to get access to abortion.
sentences.zh: 也是禁止堕胎州的女性仍然能够获得堕胎服务的主要原因。

sentences.en: Okay, so let's talk about SHIELD laws.
sentences.zh: 好的，那我们来谈谈“盾牌法”。

sentences.en: First of all, what are they?
sentences.zh: 首先，它们是什么？

sentences.en: So almost immediately after Roe was overturned, you have conservative states, red states, putting into place abortion bans that were and are very strict.
sentences.zh: 在“罗诉韦德案”被推翻后几乎立即，保守派州，也就是红州，就开始实施非常严格的堕胎禁令。

sentences.en: So they make abortion illegal in almost all cases.
sentences.zh: 它们在几乎所有情况下都将堕胎定为非法。

sentences.en: There are a few exceptions.
sentences.zh: 只有极少数例外。

sentences.en: And they have penalties for anybody who is providing abortion, helping people travel for an abortion.
sentences.zh: 而且对于任何提供堕胎服务、帮助他人前往堕胎的人，都有惩罚措施。

sentences.en: To states where it's legal.
sentences.zh: 前往堕胎合法的州。

sentences.en: To states where it's legal.
sentences.zh: 前往堕胎合法的州。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And this raises some legal questions for providers in blue states.
sentences.zh: 这给蓝州的医疗服务提供者带来了一些法律问题。

sentences.en: Are they putting themselves at risk if they provide abortion to a patient from a red state with an abortion ban?
sentences.zh: 如果他们为来自有堕胎禁令的红州的病人提供堕胎服务，他们是否会让自己陷入风险？

sentences.en: When the Supreme Court draft opinion was leaked showing that Roe versus Wade could possibly be overturned, the state legislature here in New York acted immediately.
sentences.zh: 当最高法院的意见草案被泄露，显示“罗诉韦德案”可能被推翻时，纽约州的立法机构立即采取了行动。

sentences.en: Welcome back.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回来。

sentences.en: Another step in making California a sanctuary for abortion.
sentences.zh: 这是使加州成为堕胎避难所的又一步。

sentences.en: Oregon lawmakers are working on a bill that would further protect the right to abortion in Oregon.
sentences.zh: 俄勒冈州的立法者正在制定一项法案，将进一步保护俄勒冈州的堕胎权。

sentences.en: Senate Bill 1 ensures a woman's right to choose an abortion in Hawaii, protects health care workers.
sentences.zh: 参议院第1号法案确保了夏威夷女性选择堕胎的权利，并保护医护人员。

sentences.en: So what starts to develop are these laws which basically say, if you provide an abortion to a patient from a state with an abortion ban, we will protect you.
sentences.zh: 所以开始出现这些法律，基本内容是：如果你为来自有堕胎禁令州的病人提供堕胎服务，我们将保护你。

sentences.en: Hence, shield law.
sentences.zh: 因此得名“盾牌法”。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And how exactly do these shield laws say they would protect the providers?
sentences.zh: 那么这些“盾牌法”究竟是如何保护医疗服务提供者的呢？

sentences.en: So a shield law is basically a cooperation blockade.
sentences.zh: “盾牌法”基本上是一种合作封锁。

sentences.en: So it says here in our shield law state, we will not cooperate with another state that is trying to sue or prosecute a resident in our state who isn't involved in an abortion.
sentences.zh: 它规定在我们实行“盾牌法”的州，我们不会配合其他州试图起诉或控告我们州内参与堕胎的居民。

sentences.en: So that's really starkly different from the way states usually do cooperate.
sentences.zh: 这与各州通常的合作方式截然不同。

sentences.en: And usually, you know, one state files charges against somebody in another state.
sentences.zh: 通常情况下，一个州会对另一个州的人提起指控。

sentences.en: And the state where that person is will extradite that person, will share records, will respond to subpoenas.
sentences.zh: 而该人所在的州会将其引渡，分享记录，并响应传票。

sentences.en: But under shield laws, abortion providers and people involved in providing abortions to people from red states are protected.
sentences.zh: 但在“盾牌法”下，堕胎服务提供者和参与为红州居民提供堕胎服务的人员受到保护。

sentences.en: And the officials in those shield law states are required not to cooperate, not to extradite.
sentences.zh: 这些“盾牌法”州的官员被要求不得配合，不得引渡。

sentences.en: So even though these providers are doing something that is legal in their state, those states are being extra cautious, right?
sentences.zh: 所以即使这些服务提供者做的事情在他们州是合法的，这些州也格外谨慎，对吧？

sentences.en: They're basically saying, hey, don't worry, we are not going to let you get into trouble.
sentences.zh: 他们基本上是在说，嘿，别担心，我们不会让你惹上麻烦。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So the first shield law that passed protected providers who served patients who traveled from states with abortion bans to the blue state.
sentences.zh: 所以第一部通过的“盾牌法”保护的是那些为从堕胎禁令州前往蓝州的病人提供服务的医疗人员。

sentences.en: But of course, providers in blue states who were making abortion available to people who came to them were only serving part of the need for abortion access.
sentences.zh: 但当然，蓝州那些为前来求助的人提供堕胎服务的医疗人员，只满足了部分堕胎需求。

sentences.en: A lot of women seeking abortions can't travel for one reason or another.
sentences.zh: 许多寻求堕胎的女性因为各种原因无法长途跋涉。

sentences.en: It's expensive.
sentences.zh: 这很昂贵。

sentences.en: It's very time consuming.
sentences.zh: 而且非常耗时。

sentences.en: And there's also, you know, explaining to everybody around them in their community, why are you suddenly leaving the state for a few days?
sentences.zh: 而且还有，你知道，要向社区周围的人解释，为什么你突然要离开州几天？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: It's not just like money and time and child care, which I guess is maybe a form of money and time, but it's also about privacy.
sentences.zh: 这不仅仅是金钱、时间和育儿问题，虽然我想这可能也是金钱和时间的一种形式，但这还关乎隐私。

sentences.en: Who needs to be involved in this process?
sentences.zh: 谁需要参与这个过程？

sentences.en: Who do you have to tell?
sentences.zh: 你必须告诉谁？

sentences.en: Who needs to know about something that is, for many women, very deeply private?
sentences.zh: 谁需要知道这件事？对许多女性来说，这是非常深层的隐私。

sentences.en: And for many women, there is an easier and more preferable pathway to getting an abortion.
sentences.zh: 对许多女性来说，有一种更容易、更可取的堕胎途径。

sentences.en: And that's through abortion medication early in pregnancy.
sentences.zh: 那就是通过怀孕早期的药物流产。

sentences.en: And this has become a much more common way of getting an abortion, so much so that even before Roe was
sentences.zh: 这已经成为一种更常见的堕胎方式，以至于在“罗诉韦德案”被推翻之前，

sentences.en: overturned, more than half of abortions in this country were being carried out with abortion pills.
sentences.zh: 美国超过一半的堕胎是通过堕胎药进行的。

sentences.en: Those pills, just to be clear, are the drugs mifepristone and misoprostol.
sentences.zh: 明确一下，这些药是米非司酮和米索前列醇。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And before the pandemic, the FDA had regulations that required patients to go to a doctor or another abortion provider to pick up the mifepristone, the first drug, in person.
sentences.zh: 在疫情之前，FDA有规定，要求患者必须亲自去看医生或其他堕胎服务提供者，才能领取第一种药物米非司酮。

sentences.en: And that, of course, was limiting for people.
sentences.zh: 当然，这对人们来说是一种限制。

sentences.en: Not everybody can go to a clinic.
sentences.zh: 不是每个人都能去诊所。

sentences.en: Not every doctor is a certified prescriber.
sentences.zh: 也不是每个医生都是认证的处方医生。

sentences.en: But during the pandemic, the FDA started to change those rules and allowed the medications to be prescribed
sentences.zh: 但在疫情期间，FDA开始改变这些规则，允许通过远程医疗开具药物，

sentences.en: by telemedicine without seeing a doctor and mailed to wherever the patient was.
sentences.zh: 无需看医生，并邮寄到患者所在的任何地方。

sentences.en: So after Roe was overturned, there was a realization that you could send abortion pills in the mail, to any state, including states with bans.
sentences.zh: 所以“罗诉韦德案”被推翻后，人们意识到可以将堕胎药邮寄到任何州，包括有禁令的州。

sentences.en: And that's why several states start to adopt either new shield laws or amended shield laws
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么几个州开始采用新的“盾牌法”或修订后的“盾牌法”，

sentences.en: that explicitly say that they will protect an abortion provider who is prescribing and sending abortion pills through the mail to patients in states with bans.
sentences.zh: 明确规定它们将保护那些为有禁令州的患者开具并邮寄堕胎药的堕胎服务提供者。

sentences.en: So instead of providers just treating women who come to their states where abortion is legal, what you've described is abortion providers essentially bringing the abortion to these
sentences.zh: 所以，医疗服务提供者不再仅仅是治疗来到他们合法堕胎州的女性，你所描述的是堕胎服务提供者实际上把堕胎服务带到了这些

sentences.en: women in their states where abortion is not legal.
sentences.zh: 堕胎不合法的州的女性身边。

sentences.en: And I think that sounds pretty risky for the providers, no?
sentences.zh: 我觉得这对医疗服务提供者来说听起来风险很大，不是吗？

sentences.en: It's definitely riskier for the providers for sure.
sentences.zh: 对医疗服务提供者来说，这绝对风险更大。

sentences.en: I think these types of laws are really unusual and they really haven't been tested.
sentences.zh: 我认为这类法律非常罕见，而且确实还没有经过考验。

sentences.en: So it's a question whether they will ultimately stand.
sentences.zh: 所以它们最终能否站得住脚还是个问题。

sentences.en: I think that's why you don't see that many abortion providers doing it.
sentences.zh: 我想这就是为什么你没看到那么多堕胎服务提供者这样做。

sentences.en: It takes a kind of special personality and somebody who's comfortable with that level of risk.
sentences.zh: 这需要一种特殊的性格，并且需要能够承受那种程度风险的人。

sentences.en: Many of these providers are people who are kind of more advanced in their careers and maybe their children are grown and they just feel like they have a little bit less to lose.
sentences.zh: 许多这样的服务提供者在职业生涯中处于较高级阶段，也许他们的孩子已经长大，他们觉得没什么可失去的。

sentences.en: Usually some of them have kind of protected their assets and put them in truSt.
sentences.zh: 通常他们中的一些人已经保护了自己的资产，并将其放入信托中。

sentences.en: But still, they are absolutely taking a lot of chances and they know that.
sentences.zh: 但即便如此，他们绝对是在冒很大的风险，他们也知道这一点。

sentences.en: They're well aware of that.
sentences.zh: 他们非常清楚这一点。

sentences.en: I mean, they go into this eyes open because they are really very committed to providing this access and they see it as a really important avenue.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们睁大眼睛进入这个领域，因为他们真的非常致力于提供这种服务，并将其视为一条非常重要的途径。

sentences.en: And it has become that.
sentences.zh: 它也确实成为了这样。

sentences.en: Shield law providers are now sending probably more than 10,000 pills a month to women in states with abortion bans.
sentences.zh: “盾牌法”下的服务提供者现在每月可能向有堕胎禁令州的女性寄送超过10,000份药物。

sentences.en: I know, Pam, that we've said on the show before that since Dobbs, abortions have actually gone up, which feels kind of surprising.
sentences.zh: 帕姆，我知道我们在节目中说过，自“多布斯案”以来，堕胎数量实际上有所上升，这感觉有点令人惊讶。

sentences.en: Is this the reason why?
sentences.zh: 这是原因吗？

sentences.en: This is part of the reason.
sentences.zh: 这是原因之一。

sentences.en: And these shield laws have put red states in a situation where they are trying to figure out how to stop these medications from flowing into their states.
sentences.zh: 这些“盾牌法”使红州陷入了一种境地，他们正试图找出如何阻止这些药物流入他们州的方法。

sentences.en: And for a while, they've been looking for cases that would allow them to try to challenge these shield laws.
sentences.zh: 有一段时间，他们一直在寻找能够让他们挑战这些“盾牌法”的案件。

sentences.en: And eventually they found it.
sentences.zh: 最终他们找到了。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: I'm Wynna Liu.
sentences.zh: 我是温娜·刘。

sentences.en: I write the game Connections, one of the puzzles from New York Times games.
sentences.zh: 我编写《纽约时报》游戏中的拼图游戏《Connections》。

sentences.en: And I love horror movies.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢恐怖电影。

sentences.en: I love my dog.
sentences.zh: 我爱我的狗。

sentences.en: And I love trying to trick you.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢尝试捉弄你们。

sentences.en: I'm Sam Mazursky.
sentences.zh: 我是萨姆·马祖斯基。

sentences.en: And I create the game Spelling Bee and Letterboxd on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 我每天制作《Spelling Bee》和《Letterboxd》游戏。

sentences.en: And I have this thing called promesthesia.
sentences.zh: 我有一种叫“联觉”的东西。

sentences.en: I see color when I'm listening to music.
sentences.zh: 我听音乐时能看到颜色。

sentences.en: New York Times games are made by people like the ones you just heard from.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》游戏是由刚才你们听到的那些人制作的。

sentences.en: Go to nytimes.com slash games to start playing today.
sentences.zh: 前往nytimes.com/games，今天就开始玩吧。

sentences.en: Pam, tell us about the case that you mentioned before the break.
sentences.zh: 帕姆，告诉我们你刚才提到的那个案件。

sentences.en: The one that anti-abortion activists have been waiting for.
sentences.zh: 那个反堕胎活动人士一直在等待的案件。

sentences.en: Who was involved?
sentences.zh: 谁参与其中？

sentences.en: What was it about?
sentences.zh: 它是关于什么的？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So it's actually two cases from two different states.
sentences.zh: 其实这是来自两个不同州的两个案件。

sentences.en: They just happen to involve the same New York doctor, Dr. Margaret Carpenter.
sentences.zh: 它们恰好涉及同一位纽约医生，玛格丽特·卡彭特医生。

sentences.en: Dr. Carpenter lives in New Paltz, New York.
sentences.zh: 卡彭特医生住在纽约州新帕尔茨。

sentences.en: And she has been a longtime reproductive health provider.
sentences.zh: 她是一位长期的生殖健康服务提供者。

sentences.en: And under S.H.i.e.L.D.
sentences.zh: And under S.H.i.e.L.D.

sentences.en: laws, she's been prescribing abortion pills to patients in all 50 states.
sentences.zh: 法律，她一直在为全美50个州的患者开具堕胎药。

sentences.en: A New York doctor faces a penalty after allegedly prescribing abortion pills to a Texas resident.
sentences.zh: 一名纽约医生在涉嫌为德克萨斯州居民开具堕胎药后面临处罚。

sentences.en: Tonight, Attorney General Ken Paxton is suing a doctor in New York who prescribes.
sentences.zh: 今晚，总检察长肯·帕克斯顿正在起诉一名开具处方的纽约医生。

sentences.en: This is one of the first challenges of the so-called S.H.i.e.L.D.
sentences.zh: 这是对所谓“盾牌法”的首次挑战之一，

sentences.en: laws, and it sets up a fight between Texas and New York.
sentences.zh: 它引发了德克萨斯州和纽约州之间的斗争。

sentences.en: So the first case is actually a civil suit that was brought against Dr. Carpenter.
sentences.zh: 所以第一个案件实际上是对卡彭特医生提起的民事诉讼。

sentences.en: And that suit accuses Dr. Carpenter of prescribing and sending abortion medication to a 20-year-old woman in Texas last summer.
sentences.zh: 该诉讼指控卡彭特医生去年夏天为德克萨斯州一名20岁女性开具并寄送了堕胎药。

sentences.en: And it says that after the woman took the pills, she asked her partner to take her to the emergency room because she was bleeding.
sentences.zh: 诉讼称，该女子服药后，因为出血，要求伴侣带她去急诊室。

sentences.en: Now,
sentences.zh: 现在，

sentences.en: it's worth noting that medication abortion is very safe and that bleeding is part of what happens during a medication abortion process because it is the pregnancy tissue being expelled.
sentences.zh: 值得注意的是，药物流产非常安全，出血是药物流产过程的一部分，因为这是妊娠组织被排出。

sentences.en: And so it's not that uncommon for women to wonder if they're bleeding at an appropriate level.
sentences.zh: 所以女性想知道她们的出血量是否正常并不罕见。

sentences.en: And there, apparently, her partner learned that she was nine weeks pregnant and he suspected that she wasn't just having a miscarriage.
sentences.zh: 显然，她的伴侣在那里得知她怀孕九周了，他怀疑她不仅仅是流产。

sentences.en: So he went back to their home and he found the medications with Dr. Carpenter's name on the prescription and he reported this to the attorney general's office.
sentences.zh: 所以他回到家，发现了处方上写着卡彭特医生名字的药物，并向总检察长办公室举报了此事。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: In a statement, Paxton said, in Texas, we treasure the health and lives of mothers and babies.
sentences.zh: 帕克斯顿在一份声明中说，在德克萨斯州，我们珍视母亲和婴儿的健康与生命。

sentences.en: And so in December of last year, the attorney general of Texas sued Dr. Carpenter for basically violating Texas's abortion ban.
sentences.zh: 因此，去年12月，德克萨斯州总检察长起诉卡彭特医生违反了德克萨斯州的堕胎禁令。

sentences.en: And so under the S.H.i.e.L.D.
sentences.zh: 根据“盾牌法”，

sentences.en: law, Dr. Carpenter and her lawyers did not respond to the civil suit.
sentences.zh: 卡彭特医生和她的律师没有回应这起民事诉讼。

sentences.en: They didn't show up in court.
sentences.zh: 他们没有出庭。

sentences.en: They didn't file any sort of response.
sentences.zh: 他们没有提交任何形式的答复。

sentences.en: And so as a result,
sentences.zh: 因此，

sentences.en: a judge in the case has ordered a fine of about $113,000 and also issued a permanent injunction that says Dr. Carpenter is prevented from sending abortion pills to patients in Texas again.
sentences.zh: 该案法官下令处以约113,000美元的罚款，并发布了一项永久禁令，禁止卡彭特医生再次向德克萨斯州的患者寄送堕胎药。

sentences.en: So Dr. Carpenter's strategy is essentially trust the S.H.i.e.L.D.
sentences.zh: 所以卡彭特医生的策略本质上是相信“盾牌法”，

sentences.en: law and ignore what's happening in Texas.
sentences.zh: 并无视德克萨斯州正在发生的事情。

sentences.en: So what is Texas's strategy to get her to pay the fine?
sentences.zh: 那么德克萨斯州打算采取什么策略让她支付罚款呢？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So this is where the showdown with the S.H.i.e.L.D.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是与“盾牌法”对抗的切入点，

sentences.en: law is being set up, right?
sentences.zh: 对吧？

sentences.en: Texas judge issues a punishment and now Texas wants to enforce its punishment.
sentences.zh: 德克萨斯州的法官下达了处罚，现在德州想要执行这一处罚。

sentences.en: And so this spring, the state of Texas goes to New York, to the county where Dr. Carpenter lives, and it tries to file a document that says,
sentences.zh: 因此，今年春天，德克萨斯州前往纽约，来到卡彭特医生居住的县，试图提交一份文件，上面写着：

sentences.en: we are asking you in New York to compel Dr. Carpenter to pay up and to honor the injunction.
sentences.zh: 我们要求你们纽约方面强制卡彭特医生支付罚款并遵守禁令。

sentences.en: And the New York clerk says, hold up.
sentences.zh: 而纽约的书记官说，等等。

sentences.en: No, we are not even accepting this court document from you.
sentences.zh: 不，我们甚至不会接受你们提交的这份法庭文件。

sentences.en: We're not even going to let you establish a case number here.
sentences.zh: 我们甚至不会让你们在这里立案。

sentences.en: We are just, you know, not having it under the S.H.i.e.L.D.
sentences.zh: 你知道，根据“盾牌法”，

sentences.en: law.
sentences.zh: 我们就是不予受理。

sentences.en: We have a little surprise to hear that a local clerk would know about this law and also be able to, like, unilaterally stand up to a judgment like this.
sentences.zh: 听到当地书记官竟然了解这项法律，并且能够单方面抵制这样的判决，我们感到有些惊讶。

sentences.en: Should I be surprised or is that just ignorance on my part?
sentences.zh: 我应该感到惊讶吗？还是说这只是我的孤陋寡闻？

sentences.en: Well, it's definitely an unusual thing for a county clerk to be doing in most cases.
sentences.zh: 嗯，在大多数情况下，县书记官这样做确实很不寻常。

sentences.en: But in this situation, New York has been one of the states that has really made a big deal out of their S.H.i.e.L.D.
sentences.zh: 但在这种情况下，纽约州一直是非常重视其“盾牌法”的州之一，

sentences.en: law and their determination to protect abortion rights in this way.
sentences.zh: 他们决心以这种方式保护堕胎权。

sentences.en: And so they have educated and trained officials across the state to be ready if something like this comes across their desk.
sentences.zh: 因此，他们对全州的官员进行了教育和培训，让他们在遇到此类情况时做好准备。

sentences.en: In this case, the county clerk was ready and said, sorry, we are stopping you before you even reach the courthouse door.
sentences.zh: 在这种情况下，县书记官已经做好了准备，并表示：抱歉，在你们到达法院门口之前，我们就已经把你们拦下了。

sentences.en: So right now we have a legal standoff, right?
sentences.zh: 所以现在我们陷入了法律僵局，对吧？

sentences.en: We have a civil judgment in Texas that Texas is not able to enforce.
sentences.zh: 我们在德克萨斯州有一个民事判决，但德州却无法执行。

sentences.en: And what about the other case against Dr. Carpenter that you mentioned?
sentences.zh: 那么你提到的针对卡彭特医生的另一起案件呢？

sentences.en: What's that one about?
sentences.zh: 那起案件是怎么回事？

sentences.en: Yeah, so that case is from Louisiana, and it's a criminal case that was brought in January of this year.
sentences.zh: 是的，那起案件来自路易斯安那州，是一起今年一月提起的刑事案件。

sentences.en: And in that case, a grand jury in Louisiana indicted Dr. Carpenter on charges of providing abortion-inducing drugs.
sentences.zh: 在那起案件中，路易斯安那州的一个大陪审团以提供堕胎药物的罪名起诉了卡彭特医生。

sentences.en: And, you know, as with the Texas case, we really don't know a lot of details about the Louisiana case.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，和德州的案件一样，我们对路易斯安那州案件的细节了解并不多。

sentences.en: The description of what happened is coming directly from authorities in the states themselves.
sentences.zh: 关于所发生事件的描述直接来自各州当局。

sentences.en: So it's just worth noting that they are painting a picture of how these cases unfolded in a particular way, and we don't independently know if what they're saying is accurate.
sentences.zh: 所以值得注意的是，他们所描绘的案件发展过程带有特定倾向，我们无法独立核实他们所说的是否准确。

sentences.en: What the district attorney in Louisiana has said is that there was a teenager, someone under 18, her mother helped her order abortion pills.
sentences.zh: 路易斯安那州的地区检察官表示，有一名未成年少女（18岁以下），她的母亲帮助她订购了堕胎药。

sentences.en: It turned out that Dr. Carpenter was the prescriber and mailed those pills.
sentences.zh: 结果发现卡彭特医生是处方开具者，并将这些药寄了出去。

sentences.en: And the district attorney says that the teenager was sort of pressed by her mother to take the abortion pills.
sentences.zh: 地区检察官称，这名少女是在其母亲的某种压力下服用了堕胎药。

sentences.en: And then at some point, the teenager called 911 and was taken to a hospital.
sentences.zh: 后来，这名少女拨打了911并被送往医院。

sentences.en: We don't really know why.
sentences.zh: 我们并不真正了解原因。

sentences.en: And that's where authorities learned that she had taken abortion pills.
sentences.zh: 当局就是在那时得知她服用了堕胎药的。

sentences.en: Let me be clear what this case is about.
sentences.zh: 让我明确一下这起案件的性质。

sentences.en: This is about a case in which a minor in Louisiana got pregnant.
sentences.zh: 这是一起路易斯安那州未成年人怀孕的案件。

sentences.en: Dr. Carpenter has been indicted for providing this medication.
sentences.zh: 卡彭特医生因提供这种药物而被起诉。

sentences.en: And the mother of the teenager has also been indicted and has pleaded not guilty.
sentences.zh: 这名少女的母亲也已被起诉，并已表示不认罪。

sentences.en: Her mom conspired with a New York doctor to get a chemical abortion pill in the mail and then forced that minor to take it.
sentences.zh: 她的母亲与一位纽约医生串通，通过邮寄方式获取了化学堕胎药，然后强迫那名未成年人服用。

sentences.en: There's only one right answer in this situation, and it's that that doctor must face extradition to Louisiana, where she can stay in trial and justice will be served.
sentences.zh: 在这种情况下，只有一个正确的答案，那就是那位医生必须面临引渡到路易斯安那州，在那里接受审判，以伸张正义。

sentences.en: So when one person in one state is indicted by another state, then that state that's indicted them tries to extradite them,
sentences.zh: 所以，当一个人在一个州被另一个州起诉时，那个起诉他们的州就会试图引渡他们，

sentences.en: tries to get them to come in and face the criminal charges in court because otherwise that case can't proceed.
sentences.zh: 试图让他们出庭面对刑事指控，因为否则案件就无法推进。

sentences.en: You know, criminal cases, different from civil cases, the defendant has to be there.
sentences.zh: 你知道，刑事案件与民事案件不同，被告必须到场。

sentences.en: So if she doesn't show up and they don't try to force her to show up, then it won't proceed.
sentences.zh: 所以如果她不出现，而他们也不设法强制她出庭，那么案件就不会推进。

sentences.en: Louisiana has done that.
sentences.zh: 路易斯安那州已经这样做了。

sentences.en: They've issued an extradition warrant.
sentences.zh: 他们签发了引渡令。

sentences.en: Which, as you've told us, is going to be hard to execute from a blue state that has a shield law.
sentences.zh: 正如你告诉我们的，在一个拥有“盾牌法”的蓝色州，这很难执行。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Louisiana has changed their laws, but that has no bearing on the laws here in the state of New York.
sentences.zh: 路易斯安那州修改了他们的法律，但这与纽约州的法律毫无关系。

sentences.en: New York's governor, Kathy Hochul, has made this a real strong point.
sentences.zh: 纽约州州长凯西·霍楚尔对此立场非常坚定。

sentences.en: I took an oath of office to protect all New Yorkers, and I will uphold not only our Constitution, but the laws of our land.
sentences.zh: 我宣誓就职是为了保护所有纽约人，我不仅要维护我们的宪法，还要维护我们州的法律。

sentences.en: And I will not be signing an extradition order that came from the governor of Louisiana.
sentences.zh: 我不会签署来自路易斯安那州州长的引渡令。

sentences.en: Not now, not ever.
sentences.zh: 现在不会，以后也不会。

sentences.en: She said, no way, no how.
sentences.zh: 她说，绝不可能，想都别想。

sentences.en: We are not sending Dr. Carpenter to Louisiana.
sentences.zh: 我们不会把卡彭特医生送到路易斯安那州。

sentences.en: So that's where the case stands at the moment.
sentences.zh: 这就是目前案件的状况。

sentences.en: Again, sort of a standoff.
sentences.zh: 再次强调，这是一种僵局。

sentences.en: It's possible that Louisiana will try to go to a New York court and challenge New York's refusal to extradite.
sentences.zh: 路易斯安那州可能会尝试向纽约法院提起诉讼，挑战纽约拒绝引渡的决定。

sentences.en: But they haven't done that yet.
sentences.zh: 但他们目前还没有这样做。

sentences.en: But it certainly sends a chilling shot across the bow to all the other shield law providers who are doing this.
sentences.zh: 但这无疑给所有其他正在从事此类工作的“盾牌法”保护下的医疗提供者敲响了警钟。

sentences.en: I actually want to ask you about that shot across the bow thing because I'm really curious how people in the abortion access space are interpreting what's happening with these two cases.
sentences.zh: 我其实想问问关于“敲响警钟”的事，因为我很好奇堕胎服务领域的人们是如何解读这两起案件的。

sentences.en: Because in both of them, it feels like at least for now, New York's shield law is kind of standing in the way of Texas and Louisiana prevailing.
sentences.zh: 因为在这两起案件中，至少目前看来，纽约的“盾牌法”似乎阻碍了德克萨斯州和路易斯安那州的胜诉。

sentences.en: But as you've said, the anti-abortion activists are trying to use these cases to challenge the shield law in New York.
sentences.zh: 但正如你所说，反堕胎活动人士正试图利用这些案件来挑战纽约的“盾牌法”。

sentences.en: And so I'm curious, what is the next step for Texas and Louisiana to potentially continue to challenge this?
sentences.zh: 所以我很好奇，德克萨斯州和路易斯安那州下一步可能采取什么行动来继续挑战这一法律？

sentences.en: Yeah, I think most people expect that there will be a next step, that these are supposed to be test cases to basically try to undercut the protection of shield laws.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为大多数人都预料到会有下一步行动，这些案件旨在作为测试案例，基本上是为了削弱“盾牌法”的保护力度。

sentences.en: So most people expect that Texas and or Louisiana will keep pursuing this.
sentences.zh: 所以大多数人预计德克萨斯州和/或路易斯安那州会继续追究此事。

sentences.en: They will end up in federal court, possibly the Supreme Court, and they will try to say that the shield laws are unconstitutional.
sentences.zh: 他们最终会闹到联邦法院，甚至可能是最高法院，并试图宣称“盾牌法”违宪。

sentences.en: And there may also be a challenge to the question of whether a state can decide not to extradite someone who's been criminally charged in another state.
sentences.zh: 此外，对于一个州是否可以决定不引渡在另一个州被刑事起诉的人，也可能会受到挑战。

sentences.en: So basically, this is going to end up as a showdown where this whole concept of shield laws, which is largely untested,
sentences.zh: 所以基本上，这最终将演变成一场对决，而“盾牌法”这一概念在很大程度上尚未经过检验，

sentences.en: will end up being run through the mill of the federal courts and we'll see if they're allowed to stand.
sentences.zh: 最终将不得不经过联邦法院的审理，看看它们是否能站得住脚。

sentences.en: On what basis will the red states even try to challenge these laws?
sentences.zh: 红州将以什么为依据来挑战这些法律？

sentences.en: So there are a few different legal arguments that the states can use,
sentences.zh: 州政府可以使用几种不同的法律论点，

sentences.en: but the one that seems to come up the most often is that the Constitution requires states to basically respect each other's laws.
sentences.zh: 但最常被提及的一个是宪法要求各州基本上尊重彼此的法律。

sentences.en: They have to cooperate with each other.
sentences.zh: 他们必须相互合作。

sentences.en: And in this case, the provision that they cite is called the full faith in credit clause.
sentences.zh: 在这种情况下，他们引用的条款被称为“完全信任与信用条款”。

sentences.en: I mean, I understand that, right, because the alternative would probably be chaos, like if states could just pick and choose what other states' laws they were going to respect.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我理解这一点，因为如果各州可以随意选择尊重其他州的哪些法律，那后果恐怕会是一片混乱。

sentences.en: So I do wonder, what do blue states say in response to that?
sentences.zh: 所以我确实想知道，蓝州对此有何回应？

sentences.en: Well, there are exceptions to the full faith in credit clause.
sentences.zh: 嗯，“完全信任与信用条款”是有例外的。

sentences.en: And one of those exceptions is that if one state has a really deeply held public policy objective, that public policy objective overrides a contradictory law in another state.
sentences.zh: 其中一个例外是，如果一个州有非常深厚的公共政策目标，那么该公共政策目标可以凌驾于另一个州的矛盾法律之上。

sentences.en: That's going to be one way that the legal argument is going to play out.
sentences.zh: 这将是法律论点展开的一种方式。

sentences.en: There could be others.
sentences.zh: 可能还有其他方式。

sentences.en: I would expect lawyers on both sides of this argument to be very creative and to think of lots of different legal and procedural routes once it comes to federal court,
sentences.zh: 我预计双方的律师在进入联邦法院后，会非常有创意地思考各种不同的法律和程序途径，

sentences.en: because that's what we've seen with other abortion cases.
sentences.zh: 因为我们在其他堕胎案件中已经看到了这一点。

sentences.en: I realize that shield laws are not of the Supreme Court yet, and they would take a really long time to wind their way there.
sentences.zh: 我意识到“盾牌法”尚未上诉到最高法院，而且要走到那一步需要很长时间。

sentences.en: But if they do make it in front of SCOTUS, and if SCOTUS does decide that shield laws are unconstitutional, I wonder what happens to Dr. Carpenter.
sentences.zh: 但如果它们真的出现在最高法院面前，且最高法院裁定“盾牌法”违宪，我想知道卡彭特医生会怎样。

sentences.en: And I also wonder what happens to abortion just generally across the country.
sentences.zh: 我也想知道全国的堕胎问题总体上会发生什么。

sentences.en: Well, you know, of course, we don't know exactly what would happen to Dr. Carpenter, but the charges and the cases against her could result in jail time,
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道，当然我们不知道卡彭特医生具体会遭遇什么，但针对她的指控和案件可能会导致监禁、

sentences.en: steep financial penalty and preventing her from continuing this work.
sentences.zh: 高额经济处罚，并阻止她继续这项工作。

sentences.en: And if we were to see these shield laws get struck down by the Supreme Court, then things will be different.
sentences.zh: 如果我们看到这些“盾牌法”被最高法院推翻，那么情况就会不同了。

sentences.en: Certainly some providers who are sending abortion pills to states with bans will stop doing that.
sentences.zh: 当然，一些向有禁令的州发送堕胎药的医疗提供者会停止这样做。

sentences.en: Others will probably continue, even though they'd be taking even greater risk than they're taking now.
sentences.zh: 其他人可能会继续，尽管他们承担的风险比现在更大。

sentences.en: And the abortion landscape in America that's already been rewritten after Roe was overturned is going to be rewritten once again.
sentences.zh: 而美国在“罗诉韦德案”被推翻后已经重塑的堕胎格局，将再次被重塑。

sentences.en: And I think we're going to see even starker divisions between states with abortion bans and states that protect abortion.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们将看到禁止堕胎的州与保护堕胎的州之间出现更鲜明的对立。

sentences.en: But even if the Supreme Court upholds the legality of shield laws,
sentences.zh: 但即使最高法院维持了“盾牌法”的合法性，

sentences.en: that doesn't mean that the practice of sending abortion pills to states with abortion bans is just going to continue without additional ways to challenge it.
sentences.zh: 也不意味着向禁止堕胎的州发送堕胎药的做法就能在没有其他挑战方式的情况下继续下去。

sentences.en: So you're likely to see anti-abortion advocates looking for new ways to try to stop access to abortion pills,
sentences.zh: 所以你很可能会看到反堕胎倡导者寻找新的方法来试图阻止堕胎药的获取，

sentences.en: and you're likely to see abortion rights advocates looking for new ways to try to protect and expand access to abortion pills.
sentences.zh: 你也很可能会看到堕胎权倡导者寻找新的方法来试图保护和扩大堕胎药的获取途径。

sentences.en: Pam, when the Supreme Court overturned Roe v.
sentences.zh: 帕姆，当最高法院推翻“罗诉韦德案”时，

sentences.en: Wade, part of the idea at the time was that they would just send back to the states this decision about how to handle abortion.
sentences.zh: 当时的想法之一是，他们会将如何处理堕胎的决定权交还给各州。

sentences.en: So if states wanted it to be legal, they could make it legal.
sentences.zh: 所以如果各州想要合法化，他们可以使其合法化。

sentences.en: If they didn't want it to be legal, that was up to them.
sentences.zh: 如果他们不想合法化，那就由他们决定。

sentences.en: And that would settle it, was the thinking.
sentences.zh: 当时的想法是，这样就能解决问题了。

sentences.en: And you do have a patchwork of laws as a result.
sentences.zh: 结果你确实得到了一个法律拼凑的局面。

sentences.en: But what you also have are states kind of openly fighting with each other, too.
sentences.zh: 但你同时也看到了各州之间在公开地相互争斗。

sentences.en: And I just sort of wonder if you anticipated that.
sentences.zh: 我只是想知道你是否预料到了这一点。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think a lot of people who were watching this subject and familiar with it also anticipated that this would happen because, you know, when you think about it,
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为许多关注这个话题并熟悉它的人也预料到会发生这种情况，因为，你知道，当你仔细想想，

sentences.en: there just aren't very many types of medical care that differ so dramatically from state to state.
sentences.zh: 并没有多少种医疗护理在各州之间存在如此巨大的差异。

sentences.en: So it always seemed like it was going to be problematic to have one state try to ban abortion and think that that would somehow prevent women in that state from having access to abortion.
sentences.zh: 所以，让一个州试图禁止堕胎，并认为这能以某种方式阻止该州妇女获得堕胎服务，这似乎一直都是有问题的。

sentences.en: And I think what we're seeing now, this really fierce division between states, was something that a lot of people foresaw.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们现在看到的这种州与州之间极其激烈的对立，是许多人预见到的。

sentences.en: Pam, thank you so much.
sentences.zh: 帕姆，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要了解的其他新闻。

sentences.en: Over the weekend, President Trump called for an end to the war in Gaza,
sentences.zh: 周末，特朗普总统呼吁结束加沙战争，

sentences.en: capping off a week of sharp rebukes from some of Israel's closest allies since the war started more than 18 months ago.
sentences.zh: 这为自战争开始18个多月以来，以色列一些最亲密的盟友发出的为期一周的严厉谴责画上了句号。

sentences.en: In Israel, we've been talking to them and we want to see if we can stop that whole situation as quickly as possible.
sentences.zh: 在以色列，我们一直在与他们沟通，我们希望看看能否尽快结束整个局势。

sentences.en: The shift in tone from the president and countries including Germany, Britain,
sentences.zh: 总统以及包括德国、英国、

sentences.en: Canada and France indicate that Israel's strongest partners are beginning to lose patience with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.
sentences.zh: 加拿大和法国在内的国家语气的转变表明，以色列最强大的合作伙伴开始对本雅明·内塔尼亚胡总理失去耐心。

sentences.en: And British police arrested the driver who crashed into a crowd of people celebrating Liverpool's championship soccer club on Monday,
sentences.zh: 周一，英国警方逮捕了一名司机，他驾车冲向了庆祝利物浦足球俱乐部夺冠的人群，

sentences.en: seriously wounding two and sending dozens to the hospital.
sentences.zh: 造成两人重伤，数十人被送往医院。

sentences.en: Authorities confirmed that the suspect was a 53-year-old white male, and they asked the public, quote, not to speculate on the circumstances leading up to the collision.
sentences.zh: 当局证实嫌疑人是一名53岁的白人男性，并要求公众“不要对导致碰撞的情况进行猜测”。

sentences.en: Hundreds of thousands of people had gathered to celebrate Liverpool's victory in this year's Premier League, the top tier of English soccer.
sentences.zh: 数十万人聚集在一起庆祝利物浦在今年英超联赛中的胜利，这是英格兰足球的顶级联赛。

sentences.zh: 今天的节目由亚历克斯·斯特恩、威尔·里德和戴安娜·阮制作，玛丽·威尔逊提供了帮助。

sentences.zh: 收听节目，获取让客人感到宾至如归的建议。

sentences.en: Are they a blackout sleeper?
sentences.zh: 他们是需要全黑环境才能入睡的人吗？

sentences.en: I don't mean do they blackout to go to sleep.
sentences.zh: 我不是指他们是否会昏睡过去。

sentences.en: I mean, what kind of light do they require, because that is a very specific thing.
sentences.zh: 我是指他们需要什么样的光线，因为这是一个非常具体的问题。

sentences.en: Do they have allergies, food sensitivities?
sentences.zh: 他们有过敏症或食物敏感吗？

sentences.en: Are they coffee tea drinkers?
sentences.zh: 他们是喝咖啡还是喝茶？
